note: U2 is a spec Unit: not deployed, owning a committed contract and four CI gates. Both of its stories are cross-cutting, so several acceptance criteria belong to the Units that own the screens and the writes. Those are marked Deferred with the Unit that owns them named, rather than claimed. AC10.1.4 is the criterion behind BR1.4: it requires that a refusal not disclose whether the resource exists, without naming a status - which settles the contradiction between contract-summary's schema section (403 for both) and its implementer notes (the 404-instead-of-403 wording). Revised at review: BR1.4 strengthened to byte-identity (a uniform status still leaks through the response body), BR2.4 carries ADR-001's account-id set as well as the profile set, BR3.1 separates the authenticated refresh route from the public allowlist, BR2.2's predicate is $ref rather than an undecidable 'carries money', and BR4.3 records the FIVE downstream artifacts whose 404 hypotheses BR1.4 contradicted, all since amended. Revised again at iteration 2: new BR1.7 reconciles AC10.1.6 with contract-summary B.4, which contradict each other on whether an unsupported lens hint is ignored or refused - AC10.1.6 now traces to BR1.7 rather than to rules that say nothing about hints. Iteration 2 also added BR4.4, handing BR1.4's structural-equivalence clause to U3 as a named obligation rather than leaving it as unowned prose.

reverse.target: AC9.2.3 - the five closed classes are what let a client tell a connectivity failure from a server rejection. Also the base every Deferred AC9.2.x criterion builds on: those need a screen and a write, which a spec Unit has neither of
AC9.2.3, AC10.1.4 - retryable derived from the class at the single handler, so the client is told rather than inferring from a status

No acceptance criterion states the no-English-message rule; it comes from contract-summary and TC-15/D-43. A server-authored string cannot be localized, which in a Bangla-first UI guarantees untranslated English in front of a teacher

AC10.1.1, AC10.1.2, AC10.1.3, AC10.1.4 - the non-disclosure rule, strengthened at review from uniform STATUS to BYTE-IDENTICAL response. AC10.1.4 requires that a refusal not disclose existence; a uniform 403 carrying distinct codes satisfies the status reading and leaks everything through the body. Iteration 2 added the structural-equivalence clause: both branches perform the same lookup work, so an existence-check short-circuit cannot restore the oracle in timing with every byte identical - the same structural (never wall-clock) assertion the OTP issue path carries
NFR16 - committed schema equals generated, so a contract change is a reviewable diff and an installed client is never generated from fiction

No AC covers the schema-level money check; it originates at U1's NFR9.30. CORRECTED at review: the predicate is `$ref` to the shared Money component, not 'properties carrying money' - the latter is undecidable from a generated document and is circular, since a pattern-based selector cannot see the free-form-string defect the check exists to catch
The *_display pairing rule comes from contract-summary's OQ-6 resolution rather than an AC. Recorded in the schema so the diff gate catches a field gaining or losing its sibling

AC10.1.5, NFR14, ADR-001 - TWO field sets on one iteration: owner-private profile fields and account ids. CORRECTED at review: an earlier draft carried only the first, though ADR-001 records choosing this gate over a new mechanism precisely to carry both

AC10.1.7 - every route resolves a lens bar two SEPARATE sets: five public routes, and one authenticated lens-exempt route. CORRECTED at review: an earlier draft had a single open-ended allowlist, which invites the refresh route being marked public by whoever first hits it failing

AC10.1.7, AC10.1.8 - annotation resolution via get_type_hints, unions counted only when every member qualifies, resolution failure never swallowed. CORRECTED at review: a naive issubclass is defeated by string annotations, unions and Annotated, and the real damage is an implementer returning True on the resulting error

A policy with no AC behind it, and the most important rule in this Unit. B2 has no routes and no money endpoint, so BR2.2, BR2.3, BR2.4 and BR3.1 all iterate empty sets and pass trivially. Without a committed failing fixture per gate, B2 records four green checks that have never looked at anything

From team.md Testing Posture rather than an AC: a conformance tool validates conformance and never counts as privacy coverage, because a response wrongly carrying profile fields matches its own declaration perfectly. Stated in writing so the distinction is not lost

AC10.1.1, AC10.1.2, AC10.1.3, AC10.1.4, AC10.1.6 - no error code distinguishes the unreachable case from the absent one. Added at review: BR1.4 states the property, this names the thing most likely to break it, since each of a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code pair reads as good practice alone

AC9.2.3 - retryable:false on a 401 reconciled with refresh-then-replay. Added at review: BR1.2 derived the value without recording what it MEANS on the one status where it reads as a contradiction, which is a whole paragraph in the upstream contract

AC10.1.6, FR1.3, FR1.4, FR1.5 - the lens-hint contract. Added at review iteration 2, which found that AC10.1.6 (the server IGNORES an unsupported hint) and contract-summary B.4 (the server REFUSES it with 403 LENS_NOT_AVAILABLE) directly contradict each other, and that this Unit had picked B.4's behaviour in entities.md while carrying no rule about hints at all. FR1.4 settles it: only lenses that have data are offered, so an unsupported hint is a stale client, a bug or a probe, and silent fallback serves all three under a lens they did not name - the AC10.1.8 failure shape. The two sources agree on the half that carries the security property (the hint grants nothing, the lens is always re-derived), which is why this is a wording conflict rather than a vulnerability

A cross-Bolt obligation with no AC behind it, now DISCHARGED. BR1.4's decision contradicted FIVE downstream artifacts - B2's own DoD, the confidence hypotheses of B3, B7 and B9, and the B3 checkpoint criterion in risk-and-sequencing-rationale.md - each asserting 404 as a falsification criterion, so correct implementations would have failed them. B3's is the walking skeleton's privacy hypothesis, read at a human checkpoint. All five amended 2026-10-18 to require a byte-identical 403. The fifth was named by neither the draft nor the review and was found by sweeping the record for the value, which is the generalisable lesson

A forward obligation with no AC behind it, naming U3 as owner. BR1.4's structural-equivalence clause (added at iteration 2) requires both lookup branches to execute the same queries, but BR4.1's fixture obligation correctly excludes BR1.4 because U2 owns no lookup code - leaving the one rule in this Unit that states a requirement and assigns it to nobody. U3 owns lens resolution, is the first Unit with a lookup that can fail either way, and is the walking skeleton, so the obligation is discharged where the human checkpoint reads the privacy claim. Same B1 NFR9.32 precedent BR4.3 applies
